lessons.title: Shock Physiology: preload, pump, SVR and oxygen delivery
lessons.summary: เรียน shock โดยถาม 4 อย่าง: volume/preload, pump, vascular tone, obstruction. การรู้ physiology ช่วยเลือก fluid, vasopressor, ventilation and destination ได้ถูกกว่าใช้ BP อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) Oxygen delivery
paragraphs: DO₂ ≈ cardiac output × arterial oxygen content. Cardiac output = HR × stroke volume; oxygen content depends heavily on hemoglobin and saturation. Normal BP ไม่ได้แปลว่า perfusion ปกติ.

sections.title: 2) Hypovolemic shock
paragraphs: Low preload from hemorrhage/dehydration. Treat source + appropriate volume/blood strategy. Hemorrhage requires bleeding control, not just fluid.

sections.title: 3) Distributive shock
paragraphs: Vasodilation/maldistribution (sepsis, anaphylaxis, neurogenic). Fluid and vasopressor needs depend on cause, response and local protocol.

sections.title: 4) Cardiogenic shock
paragraphs: Pump failure: MI, myocarditis, severe arrhythmia. Excess fluid can worsen pulmonary edema; consider vasoactive/inotropic support and reperfusion/definitive care.

sections.title: 5) Obstructive shock
paragraphs: Tension pneumothorax, tamponade, massive PE impair filling/outflow. Definitive relief of obstruction is key; fluids/pressors are temporizing.

key_points: Treat shock cause, not only number
quick_review: Trend mental status, pulse, skin, BP, lactate when available

quiz.q: Tension pneumothorax causes which shock type?
quiz.explain: Tension pneumothorax reduces venous return and causes obstructive shock.

lessons.title: Sepsis & Septic Shock 2026: recognition, source, fluids, vasopressors
lessons.summary: 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign updates adult sepsis guidance and explicitly includes the immediate prehospital setting. Early recognition, source-directed care and hemodynamic reassessment remain central.

sections.title: 1) What sepsis is
paragraphs: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response to infection. Do not equate fever + tachycardia alone with sepsis; look for organ dysfunction/perfusion failure.

sections.title: 2) Prehospital recognition
paragraphs: Suspect infection + altered mentation, hypotension, tachypnea, mottling, oliguria history, elevated lactate if available. qSOFA is not a stand-alone rule-out tool.

sections.title: 3) Resuscitation thinking
paragraphs: Give oxygen for hypoxemia, obtain IV/IO if indicated, fluid strategy should be individualized and reassessed frequently; persistent hypotension may require vasopressor support per system capability.

sections.title: 4) Source & antibiotics
paragraphs: Definitive sepsis care requires timely antimicrobials and source control, but prehospital protocols vary. Pre-notification can speed in-hospital bundle execution.

sections.title: 5) Reassessment
paragraphs: Reassess BP/MAP, mental status, capillary refill, urine history, lactate trend if measured, lung exam/ultrasound and signs of fluid intolerance.

key_points: Reassess after fluid rather than fixed-volume reflex
Prehospital recognition can shorten time to treatment
quick_review: Avoid fluid overload in poor cardiac reserve

lessons.title: Hypovolemic & Hemorrhagic Shock: Volume Loss, Compensation & Resuscitation
lessons.summary: เข้าใจ compensated shock ก่อน hypotension และแยก hemorrhage จาก dehydration/third spacing.

sections.title: 1) Physiology
paragraphs: Reduced circulating volume lowers venous return/preload → stroke volume falls → sympathetic tachycardia/vasoconstriction. Hypotension can be late, especially in young patients.

sections.title: 2) Recognize perfusion failure
paragraphs: Mental status, skin, pulse quality, capillary refill, urine output (when available), shock index and trends complement BP.

sections.title: 3) Hemorrhage control first
paragraphs: Tourniquet, wound packing/direct pressure, pelvic stabilization when indicated and rapid definitive hemorrhage control matter more than chasing normal BP with crystalloid.

sections.title: 4) Fluids/blood
paragraphs: Resuscitation strategy depends on bleeding, TBI, age and local blood availability. Excess crystalloid can worsen dilution, hypothermia and tissue edema.

lessons.title: Cardiogenic Shock: Pump Failure & Mechanical Complications
lessons.summary: เมื่อหัวใจปั๊มไม่พอ การเติมน้ำแบบ reflex อาจทำให้ปอดแย่ลง.

sections.title: 1) Mechanisms
paragraphs: Large MI, severe LV/RV failure, acute MR/VSD, myocarditis and malignant arrhythmia can reduce cardiac output. High filling pressures often coexist with poor systemic perfusion.

sections.title: 2) Clinical phenotype
paragraphs: Cold/clammy, altered mental state, hypotension, weak pulse, pulmonary edema (LV) or JVD/clear lungs (isolated RV patterns). ECG and ultrasound when available help identify cause.

sections.title: 3) Resuscitation
paragraphs: Correct arrhythmia/hypoxia, evaluate ACS, use cautious fluid only when physiology suggests preload responsiveness, and vasoactive/inotropic support according to protocol/expert care.

sections.title: 4) Time-sensitive mechanical causes
paragraphs: Papillary muscle rupture, VSD, free-wall rupture/tamponade require urgent definitive intervention.

lessons.title: Obstructive Shock: PE, Tamponade & Tension Pneumothorax
lessons.summary: จำ physiology: pump may be okay but filling/outflow is mechanically blocked.

sections.title: 1) Three major emergencies
paragraphs: Massive PE obstructs pulmonary flow/RV output; tamponade prevents diastolic filling; tension pneumothorax impairs venous return and pulmonary circulation.

sections.title: 2) Pattern recognition
paragraphs: Shock with JVD and relatively clear lungs suggests obstructive/RV physiology, but findings vary. POCUS can rapidly clarify when trained/available.

sections.title: 3) Treatment is cause-specific
paragraphs: Pressors/fluids may temporize but definitive action is relieving obstruction: decompression, pericardial drainage, or reperfusion strategy for high-risk PE.

sections.title: 4) Arrest
paragraphs: PE and tension can present as PEA; reversible-cause search during arrest must be active.

lessons.title: Vasopressors & Hemodynamic Reasoning
lessons.summary: เลือก vasoactive support จาก MAP/perfusion + vascular tone + pump function ไม่ใช่จาก BP อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) MAP and organ perfusion
paragraphs: MAP is a pressure surrogate, not direct flow. A patient can have “acceptable” MAP and poor cardiac output, or low MAP with preserved mentation in selected contexts.

sections.title: 2) Receptor thinking
paragraphs: Alpha-1 increases vascular tone; beta-1 increases chronotropy/inotropy; different agents have mixed profiles. Disease phenotype and arrhythmia risk matter.

sections.title: 3) Norepinephrine concept
paragraphs: For septic vasodilatory shock, norepinephrine remains a major first-line vasopressor in contemporary guidelines once fluid strategy is addressed.

sections.title: 4) Peripheral administration
paragraphs: Modern protocols may allow carefully monitored peripheral vasopressor initiation to avoid harmful delay, using an appropriate vein, concentration and frequent site checks; follow local policy.
